verdict.rationale: ReelMimic takes a reference video (file, phone recording or YouTube link) and breaks down its shots, BPM, transitions, colors, framing and camera moves. It then plans and generates a new video modeled on that reference. However, output is limited to seven 2D drawing engines, and references that don't match a known style fall back to the closest engine. missing for 10: image-only reference input explicitly documented, true style matching beyond the seven 2D engines (no live-action or 3D), independent or hands-on corroboration of output fidelity.

support.subject: As a creator, I can point at a reference video or image and generate new footage in that style

citations.quote: A file, a phone recording or a YouTube link all work. Then tell it what you want to make.
Breaks down the reference. Shot count, shot lengths, BPM, transitions, colors, framing and camera moves.
On the home page, drop in a reference video or paste a link, say what you want, and pick Claude Code or Codex.
When a reference doesn't match a known style, it uses the closest engine and writes up a proposal for a new style.
